rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes cold spray deposition, whereas the paper used spark plasma sintering to make electrodes and then electrospark deposition to apply coatings. These are fundamentally different processes.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies cold spray at low temperature, ~200°C service, and salt spray/acidic corrosion testing. The paper used SPS at 850–1050°C, ESD under Ar, and performed no corrosion or aggressive-environment testing.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes plastic deformation, mechanical bonding, work hardening, and grain refinement without melting. The paper's mechanism relies on SPS diffusion/sintering and ESD pulsed spark melting, mixing, and rapid solidification.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance versus fusion welding and untreated surfaces. The paper predicted improved homogenization/densification with SPS temperature and more defects with more ESD layers, and did not measure wear or corrosion.
